title: Fantasmagorie
note: Chalk-line figures that turn into one another. Often called the first fully animated film.

title: Lichtspiel Opus 1
note: Among the first abstract animated films shown publicly. Shape and colour moving to music.

title: Rhythmus 21
note: Squares and rectangles on a black ground. Motion as pure rhythm, no subject.

title: Ballet Mécanique
note: Machine parts, objects and faces cut into repeating loops.

title: Symphonie Diagonale
note: Line drawings that grow and shrink along a diagonal axis.

title: Anémic Cinéma
note: Spinning spiral discs alternate with discs of spiralling puns.

title: Ghosts Before Breakfast
note: Everyday objects rebel. Trick photography used to break ordinary logic.

title: Night on Bald Mountain
note: Made on a pinscreen: thousands of pins pushed in and out to cast shadows.

title: Rhythm in Light
note: Light, reflection and objects filmed to music. Early American abstract animation.

title: A Colour Box
note: Painted straight onto film stock. Also an advert for the GPO.

title: Composition in Blue
note: Solid shapes move through a blue space in time to music.

title: Trade Tattoo
note: Offcuts of GPO documentaries, stencilled and painted over in colour.

title: An Optical Poem
note: Paper shapes on wires, timed to Liszt. Made at MGM.

title: Dots
note: Both picture and soundtrack drawn straight onto the film.

title: Motion Painting No. 1
note: One painting on glass, filmed stroke by stroke to Bach.

title: Begone Dull Care
note: Painted and scratched film cut to Oscar Peterson. Image follows sound.

title: Gerald McBoing-Boing
note: Flat, modernist cartoon style that broke away from Disney realism.

title: Blinkity Blank
note: Images scratched on black film, many shown for a single frame.

title: The Man with the Golden Arm (titles)
note: White bars on black. Often cited as the start of the modern title sequence.

title: Around the World in 80 Days (end titles)
note: A six-minute animated end sequence that retells the film.

title: Vertigo (titles)
note: Spirals drawn with a mechanical analogue computer.

title: Anatomy of a Murder (titles)
note: Cut-paper body parts animated to Ellington.

title: North by Northwest (titles)
note: Type sliding along a grid that becomes a building facade.

title: Psycho (titles)
note: Grey bars slice the type apart. Graphic form as tension.

title: Catalog
note: A showreel of effects from his analogue computer. Motion as a system.

title: Dr. No (titles)
note: Coloured dots and silhouettes. The template for every Bond opening.

title: Doctor Who (titles)
note: Video feedback, made by pointing a camera at its own monitor.

title: The Pink Panther (titles)
note: The titles introduced a character who outgrew the film.

title: Dr. Strangelove (titles)
note: Hand-drawn type laid over found footage of a B-52 refuelling.

title: Goldfinger (titles)
note: Film and credits projected onto a painted body.

title: Lapis
note: Thousands of dots form slowly turning mandalas.

title: 2001: A Space Odyssey (Star Gate)
note: Slit-scan: long exposures through a moving slit stretch light into corridors.

title: Pas de deux
note: Dancers multiplied with an optical printer. Movement left as a trail.

title: Permutations
note: Dot patterns from a digital computer, moving at related speeds.

title: Yellow Submarine
note: Pop-art animation built around the Beatles' songs.

title: Pixillation
note: Computer-generated pattern made at Bell Labs, mixed with hand animation.

title: Synchromy
note: The soundtrack shapes are also the image. You see what you hear.

title: Hunger
note: Early computer key-frame interpolation. Drawings morph into each other.

title: Arabesque
note: Harmonic motion as a design principle. Points moving at related speeds.

title: Powers of Ten
note: A continuous zoom, out and back in, by factors of ten.

title: Star Wars (opening crawl)
note: Type receding into space. Text as a physical object.

title: 3/78 (Objects and Transformations)
note: Sixteen points of light transforming. Minimal, strict, rule-based.

title: Superman (titles)
note: Streaking 3D type made with a motion-control camera.

title: Alien (titles)
note: Fragments of the title appear slowly over a dark planet.

title: MTV launch identity
note: A fixed logo shape with endlessly changing surfaces. Identity as variation.

title: Channel 4 ident
note: Coloured blocks fly together to form the 4.

title: Tron
note: One of the first feature films to use extensive computer graphics.

title: Take On Me
note: Pencil-sketch rotoscoping moving in and out of live action.

title: Luxo Jr.
note: Two desk lamps. Showed that computer animation could carry character.

title: Sledgehammer
note: Pixilation, claymation and objects animated around the singer.

title: Cape Fear (titles)
note: Water distorts type, eyes and reflections.

title: Casino (titles)
note: A body falls through the neon of Las Vegas.

title: Se7en (titles)
note: Scratched, unstable type. Made the title sequence feel like evidence.

title: Around the World
note: Each group of dancers moves to one instrument in the track.

title: Fight Club (titles)
note: A pull-back out of a brain's fear centre.

title: Six Feet Under (titles)
note: Quiet images of death and separation.

title: Catch Me If You Can (titles)
note: A flat graphic chase that openly borrows from Saul Bass.

title: Star Guitar
note: A view from a train, edited so passing buildings land on the beat.

title: Cog
note: A chain reaction of car parts, filmed for Honda.

title: Kiss Kiss Bang Bang (titles)
note: A graphic, split-screen homage to 1960s titles.

title: Dexter (titles)
note: A morning routine shot so close it reads as violence.

title: Mad Men (titles)
note: A silhouetted man falls past advertising images.

title: Magnetosphere
note: Particles driven by audio, written in Processing.

title: AANAATT
note: Physical objects shot frame by frame into geometric pattern.

title: test pattern
note: Data turned into barcode-like patterns, synchronised to sound.

title: Enter the Void (titles)
note: Fast, flashing type in many typefaces.

title: Watchmen (titles)
note: Slow-motion tableaux that retell decades of an alternate history.

title: Game of Thrones (titles)
note: A clockwork map that builds itself. Information as mechanism.

title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo (titles)
note: Liquid black bodies in a nightmare set to Immigrant Song.

title: Skyfall (titles)
note: A descent through symbols of the film's story.

title: Halt and Catch Fire (titles)
note: Circuit lines and pixel light from early computing.

title: True Detective (titles)
note: Double exposures of people and landscape.

title: Walking City
note: A walking figure that keeps changing its form without breaking stride.

title: Jessica Jones (titles)
note: Painterly, noir city images that drift between forms.

title: Order from Chaos
note: Made for Max Cooper. Rain sounds organised into rhythm and form.

title: Stranger Things (titles)
note: Kinetic typography, references to horror book and film design of the period

title: Westworld (titles)
note: Bodies and horses printed by machines.

title: Split (titles)
note: type based, a more contemporary interpretation of Saul Bass' work. or Chris kyle in the international style

title: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse
note: 3D animation drawn with print and comic-book techniques.

title: Godfather of Harlem (titles)
note: based on found footage, archive material and collage

title: Westworld (Season 3) (titles)
note: References to the Icarus mythology

title: House of the Dragon (titles)
note: Blood runs through a carved mechanism of family history.

title: Severance (titles)
note: A soft, surreal office world that bends the main character.

title: The Last of Us (titles)
note: Fungal growth spreads over maps and shapes like a pattern.
